pr_title: Fix serialization of non-ASCII-only bare strings
pr_body:
To use a binary-encoded string as a byte buffer, appended strings should be force-encoded as binary.  Otherwise, appending a non-ASCII-only string will raise `Encoding::CompatibilityError`.

Fixes #48748.

issue_context.title: Rails cache storage not working propertly
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce


1. Init new app
``` bash
rails new rails-test --main
cd rails-test
bundle add dalli
touch tmp/caching-dev.txt
```

2. Set cache store in development.rb

```ruby
config.cache_store = :mem_cache_store
```

3. Run console
``` bash
rails c
```

4. Try to write cache
```ruby
irb(main):001:0> Rails.cache.clear
Dalli::Server#connect 127.0.0.1:11211
=> [true]
irb(main):002:0> Rails.cache.write("test", "Más")
/Users/benone/.rbenv/versions/3.2.2/lib/ruby/gems/3.2.0/bundler/gems/rails-e18791c0bf2e/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/serializer_with_fallback.rb:80:in `try_dump_bare_string': incompatible character encodings: ASCII-8BIT and UTF-8 (Encoding::CompatibilityError)
```

### Expected behavior
Written cache.

### Actual behavior
Encoding::CompatibilityError Exception 

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
rails main (e18791c0bf2e)

**Ruby version**:
ruby 3.2.2 (2023-03-30 revision e51014f9c0) +YJIT [arm64-darwin22]



### Related issue:
https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/48196
comments: Thank you for the bug report! :pray:  I should have written a more end-to-end test in #48197.  This should now be fixed by #48751.

review_comments:
This always allocates, which the surrounding code seems to be trying fairly hard to avoid.

Appending `a*a*` to BARE_STRING_TEMPLATE might give the same result for free?

When I originally wrote this code, I actually wanted to use `pack("a*")` for readability.  Unfortunately, `pack("a*")` is surprisingly slow compared to `<<`.  (Perhaps it does more internal type checking of its arguments?)

<details>
  <summary>Benchmark Script</summary>

  ```ruby
  # frozen_string_literal: true

  require "benchmark/ips"

  [
    "Needs more umlaut!" * 50,
    "Needs more ümlaut!" * 50,
  ].each do |string|
    puts
    puts "=== ascii_only?: #{string.ascii_only?}"
    puts

    Benchmark.ips do |x|
      x.report('pack("a*")') do
        packed = [0, 0, 0, string].pack("CEl<a*")
      end

      x.report("string.b") do
        packed = [0, 0, 0].pack("CEl<")
        packed << string.b
      end

      x.report("string.b ?") do
        packed = [0, 0, 0].pack("CEl<")
        packed << (string.ascii_only? ? string : string.b)
      end

      x.compare!
    end
  end
  ```
</details>


It would be nice if Ruby provided a way to concatenate bytes (ignoring encoding).  Something similar was proposed in [Ruby #14975](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/14975).
